stories.title_en: Dropping a Parcel on the Road to Swap It

paragraphs.zh: 江賢，江西臨川縣人。錢本稀少，每年至七月割早穀之後，往福建崇安地方以绱鞋為生。積至年冬，約有銀一拾餘兩，收拾回家。
paragraphs.en: Jiang Xian was a man of Linchuan County, Jiangxi. He had little capital. Every year after the early rice was cut in the seventh month, he went to Chong'an in Fujian to make a living stitching shoes. By winter he had about ten-odd taels of silver and packed up to go home.

paragraphs.zh: 中途偶見一包，賢撿入手，約有銀二三兩，不勝喜悅。從前一人曰：「見者有分，不許獨得。可藏在你箱中，待僻靜處拿出來分。你撿者得二分，我見者得一分。」賢意亦肯，況銀納置彼箱，心中坦然無疑。行未數十步，忽一人忙趕到來，啼哭哀告曰：「我失銀三兩作一包，是措借納官的。你客官若拾得者，願體天心還我，陰功萬代。」前見者故作憐憫之容，曰：「是此绱鞋財主拾得，要與我均分。既是你貧苦人的，我情願不分，你可出些收贖與他，叫他把還你。」賢被此人證出，只得開箱，叫失銀者將原銀包自己取去。但得其一錢收贖，亦自以為幸；不知自銀已被棍將偽包換去矣。至晚到烏石地方，取出收贖銀還酒，將剩者欲併入大包。打開只見銅鐵，其銀一毫也無，只得大哭而罷。
paragraphs.en: On the way he happened to see a parcel. Xian picked it up; it had about two or three taels of silver. He was overjoyed. A man ahead said, "Finders share; you can't have it alone. Hide it in your chest; when we reach a quiet place we'll take it out and divide. You who picked it get two parts; I who saw it get one part." Xian was willing; besides, the silver was put in his own chest, so he felt at ease without suspicion. Before they had gone several dozen paces, suddenly a man hurried up, weeping and pleading: "I lost three taels of silver in one parcel; it was borrowed to pay the officials. If you travelers picked it up, please follow Heaven's heart and return it to me; the hidden merit will last ten thousand generations." The one who had seen it first put on a look of pity: "It was this shoe-stitching moneybags who picked it up; he wanted to split it with me. Since it's a poor man's, I'm willing not to take a share. You can give him some redemption money and tell him to return it to you." Xian, having been identified by this man, had no choice but to open the chest and tell the man who lost the silver to take the original silver parcel himself. He got one qian in redemption money and thought himself lucky; he did not know his own silver had already been swapped by the swindler for a fake parcel. That evening they reached Wushi. He took out the redemption silver to pay for wine, and wanted to put the remainder into the big parcel. He opened it and saw only copper and iron; not a hair of silver. He could only weep and let it go.

paragraphs.zh: 按：賢所賺銀，必早被棍覷見，故先偽設銀包套合。一棍在賢之先於荒僻處，俟賢來，投銀包於地。彼必撿之，乃出而欲與之分，令藏彼箱，則與彼銀共一處矣。其後棍妝情哀取，賢自應開箱還之，何自開箱使棍手親取其原包？則棍得以偽包換賢之銀，賢豈知防其脫換哉？故撿銀之時，即以其撿者與前棍均分，勿入箱中，則彼窮於計矣。然二棍亦必於僻處再搶之矣。故客路不在虛得人之有，而在密藏己之有也，斯無所失矣。
paragraphs.en: Note: The silver Xian had earned must have been spotted by the swindlers early, so they first prepared a fake silver parcel to match. One swindler went ahead of Xian to a desolate place, waited for Xian to come, and threw the silver parcel on the ground. Xian would surely pick it up; then he came out wanting to share, told him to hide it in his chest, so it was together with Xian's silver. Then the later swindler put on a pitiful act to reclaim it; Xian of course had to open the chest to return it. Why did he himself open the chest and let the swindler's hand personally take the original parcel? Then the swindler could swap a fake parcel for Xian's silver—how would Xian know to guard against the swap? So at the moment of picking up the silver, he should have split what he picked with the first swindler and not put it in the chest; then they would have been at the end of their plan. But the two swindlers would surely have robbed him again in a quiet place. So on the road as a traveler, the point is not to gain emptily what others have, but to hide tightly what one has oneself; then one will lose nothing.
